# App Guide

A shell app is a Cloudflare Worker that owns the HTML page, runs Vue SSR, and stitches fragments together.

## File Conventions

| File                    | Purpose                                                                |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `vite.config.ts`        | `defineShellConfig()` — dual build (server + client)                   |
| `application.config.ts` | `defineApplicationConfig()` — document title, styles, view transitions |
| `src/router.ts`         | Exports `routes: AppRoute[]`                                           |
| `src/pages/*.vue`       | Page components (mapped in router)                                     |
| `src/layouts/*.vue`     | Layout components — must have `<slot>`                                 |
| `src/middleware/*.ts`   | Middleware — export default function                                   |
| `wrangler.jsonc`        | Cloudflare Worker config (auto-generated service bindings)             |

## `defineApplicationConfig()`

```ts
import { defineApplicationConfig } from "framework/config";

export default defineApplicationConfig({
  document: {
    title: "My App", // <title> tag
    baseStyles: "...", // Optional — injected in <head> <style>
    viewTransitions: true, // Enable View Transitions API
  },
});
```

**`ApplicationConfig`** shape (`framework/src/config.ts`):

```ts
interface ApplicationConfig {
  document: {
    title: string;
    baseStyles?: string;
    viewTransitions?: boolean;
  };
}
```

## Routes (`src/router.ts`)

```ts
import type { AppRoute } from "framework";
import IndexPage from "./pages/index.vue";
import ProductPage from "./pages/product/[id].vue";

export const routes: AppRoute[] = [
  {
    path: "/",
    component: IndexPage,
    layout: "default",
    middleware: ["logger"],
    cache: "public, s-maxage=300, stale-while-revalidate=60",
  },
  {
    path: "/product/:id",
    component: ProductPage,
    layout: "default",
    middleware: ["logger"],
    cache: "public, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=30",
  },
];
```

**`AppRoute` fields:**

| Field        | Type        | Default     | Description                                                             |
| ------------ | ----------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `path`       | `string`    | required    | URL pattern. `:param` for dynamic segments                              |
| `component`  | `Component` | required    | Vue page component                                                      |
| `layout`     | `string`    | `'default'` | Layout name (matches filename in `src/layouts/`)                        |
| `middleware` | `string[]`  | `[]`        | Middleware names (matches filenames in `src/middleware/`)               |
| `cache`      | `string`    | —           | `Cache-Control` header on the response. Use `s-maxage` for edge caching |

## Pages

Page components are standard Vue SFCs. Dynamic params from the route are passed as props:

```
src/pages/product/[id].vue  →  route path: /product/:id  →  prop: id
```

## Layouts

Layouts wrap page content via `<slot>`. Use `<Fragment>` to embed micro-frontends:

```vue
<template>
  <Fragment id="header" />
  <main><slot /></main>
  <Fragment id="footer" />
</template>

<script setup lang="ts">
import { Fragment } from "framework";
</script>
```

The `Fragment` component renders a `<div data-fragment="..." data-props="...">` placeholder that the shell fills with SSR content from the fragment worker.

Optional `fragmentProps` for passing data:

```vue
<Fragment id="product" :fragmentProps="{ id: productId }" />
```

## Middleware

Export a default function. Return a `Response` to short-circuit:

```ts
import type { Middleware } from "framework";

const auth: Middleware = (request) => {
  if (!request.headers.get("Authorization")) {
    return new Response("Unauthorized", { status: 401 });
  }
};

export default auth;
```

Middleware runs in the order listed in `route.middleware`. If any middleware returns a `Response`, subsequent middleware and rendering are skipped.

## `wrangler.jsonc`

Auto-generated service bindings map fragments to env bindings:

```jsonc
{
  "name": "front-office",
  "main": "dist/server/entry-server.js",
  "compatibility_date": "2024-12-01",
  "compatibility_flags": ["nodejs_compat"],
  "assets": {
    "directory": "../../../dist/static",
    "binding": "ASSETS",
    "html_handling": "none",
  },
  "services": [
    { "binding": "FRAGMENT_HEADER", "service": "fragment-header" },
    { "binding": "FRAGMENT_FOOTER", "service": "fragment-footer" },
  ],
}
```

Convention: `fragment-header` → binding `FRAGMENT_HEADER`. These are auto-generated by `generateAppWranglerConfigs()` during preview/deploy — don't edit manually.
